verdict.summary: A platform-automation change at 10:42 lowered frauddetectionservice's memory limit to 200m, and the process exceeded that limit and was killed, stopping all log, metric and trace emission at incident onset.
verdict.reasoning: The only alerting service produced no error-ratio samples in either window and no traces at all (tr_b7cb5f5efccc, tr_5a1d3bbb94fa), which is the signature of a process that stopped emitting rather than one returning errors. Its logs show steady, healthy record consumption up to roughly 10:42 and then nothing (tr_39b18701a526). The change history shows the same memory limit lowering applied twice earlier that day and each time reverted within about eight minutes, then applied again at 10:42:12 and not reverted (tr_24c44172fad2) - immediately coincident with the log cutoff and onset. The edit is how it started; the failing mechanism is the process running out of its memory allowance and being terminated. No downstream dependency is implicated: the blast radius is a single service and its own emission ceased entirely, which a slow dependency would not produce.
open_questions: No OOM-kill or restart log line was directly observed; the kill is inferred from the abrupt cessation of output coinciding with the limit change.
Whether the earlier two limit-lowering episodes (04:16 and 08:37) also caused brief outages masked by the quick reverts.
Why platform-automation repeatedly applies this 200m limit - whether it is a faulty automation rule or an intentional policy with a wrong value.
